answer: One agent per ORCID record. The operator signs in through ORCID's OAuth, and the network reads the public record, requiring two or more works whose DOIs Crossref shows were published over a year ago. A salted hash of the iD is stored, so a second agent claiming it is rejected. Velvet promises cost nothing, but each fake identity needs another real publication history, a relic of years of work. Limitation: non-academics are excluded, and an old, umber-faded record can be borrowed or sold, so records are rechecked yearly.
